summary: A stone tower of 1798-99 on a bluff above a rock reef in Long Island Sound, still showing its third-order Fresnel lens from inside a Coast Guard station.

notes_for_editor: Most narrative rests on one secondary source (LighthouseFriends, paraphrased) plus USLHS roster and Bulletin/Board reports; the NRHP nomination is not digitised and the Lighthouse Board reports for 1857-1873 are not in the corpus, so those dates (1857 lens, 1867-68 repairs, 1871 siren, 1873 Florence E. Turner, 1850 Downing rescue, 1840 Lexington) are second-hand and worth a primary check. LighthouseFriends is internally inconsistent on cost (9,750 vs 9,250 on the sign) and says John Gardiner died 1812 while USLHS lists him to 1813. Boat in Downing letter named Jane in the medal inscription. Jensen 1923 and 1926 rescues: Bulletin 1926 prints Andel'sen (OCR); the 1926 Bulletin PDF page and index page 130 (index 1924-29) were matched from corpus.py page. 1899 and 1900 siren hours from Board reports are labelled by volume year; fiscal-year coverage not confirmed. Burke's USLHS record shows other stations (Four Mile Point, Faulkner's Island entries appear on the page) so his earlier career was not used. Wikipedia used for leads only. Keeper note: ready roster only partly entered (principal keepers and a few assistants); full USLHS roster has 73 lines.
